messages:
anna: Heads-up — CI showing small but consistent regression on quantized bring-up. Looks tied to synthetic promptset v3 splits.
ben: repro steps?
anna: Run I used:
```
python -m eval_runner --promptset=synthetic_cohort_v3 --model=redwood/quant-1.4 --seed=42 --split=dev
```
Log snippet:
```
[eval] examples=500 -> metric: accuracy 0.823 -> 0.810 (regression)
```
eval-bot: CI result posted: run/2026-03-20-qs-482 FAILED (regression > 1.0%)
carlos: Did the split generator change? Even a different RNG or shuffle can shift synthetic augmentation order.
diane: Which promptset SHA?
anna: promptset_sha: 0a7f3b2. I also noticed dev count is 498 locally, CI had 500 :grimacing:
ben: try `scripts/validate_split.sh` (checksums + dup ids)
anna: output:
```
$ scripts/validate_split.sh synthetic_cohort_v3 dev
FAILED: duplicate ids found: 17, 302
MISMATCH: expected 500, found 498
```
carlos: aha — duplicate ids from augmentation pass. Likely a nondet RNG in synthetic generator when run with multithread. On quant runner this surfaces because batching/reorder is different.
diane: i'll open a tiny fix to set deterministic RNG and add a test. pinging @eng-ml for visibility.
anna: can we get a canary/golden run after fix? Want to confirm quantized metric parity.
carlos: quick patch:
```
diff --git a/data/synth/generator.py b/data/synth/generator.py
- rng = np.random.RandomState()
+ rng = np.random.default_rng(FLAGS.seed)
```
ben: also add `shuffle=False` in split writer to be safe for CI golden runs
eval-bot: CI: rerun queued for run/2026-03-20-qs-482
eval-bot: CI: rerun passed — metrics within noise (accuracy 0.822 -> 0.825) :tada:
anna: nice. will add a small e2e check (count + checksum) to the eval harness to prevent regressions.
